summary.headline: FY26 revenue and profit were flat (within ±1% YoY); management sees margin improvement next year but guides only 5-10% volume growth.
summary.overview: Management described FY26 as challenging, with both top line and bottom line roughly flat YoY, and volume down about 1% and prices down about 1%. The March 2026 ammonia sourcing disruption from the Middle East war was short-lived, with inventories bridging the gap and plants kept running at roughly 60-85% utilisation. Ammonia cost rose from about INR50/kg to over INR100/kg, and the company passed through price increases, with aceto prices now above INR200/kg versus about INR140-150/kg last year. Management believes the margin trough has passed but cautioned that gains from price pass-through are temporary and that competition will settle margins later.

financial_highlights.value: Roughly flat; combined volume and price decline about 2%
About 1% above last year; capacity 2 lakh tons, output about 110,000 tons per analyst estimate (not confirmed by management)

financial_highlights.change: Up roughly 30-40% from last year's average of INR140-150/kg
Up from about INR50/kg before the war

segments.name: Ethylamines
segments.commentary: Margins have improved as alcohol prices rose and prices stabilised; management says the market is a duopoly with Balaji and has enough capacity for 4-5 years. Market share is stable.

segments.name: Methylamines
segments.commentary: Still under pressure from new capacity: Aarti Industries commissioned a plant, taking the domestic players to four (RCF, Balaji, Aarti, Alkyl Amines). Management expects overcapacity and low utilisation to persist for some time.

segments.name: Acetonitrile (aceto)
segments.commentary: Anti-dumping duty came into effect only towards end-FY26 after Chinese pipeline imports. Chinese prices have risen and imports fallen in the last quarter, with market share gains. Company has about 30,000 tons capacity across two plants and says it will be the lowest-cost producer.

segments.name: End-user mix
segments.commentary: Pharma is 50-60% of sales and agro 15-20%, together about 70-75%. Management sees no pharma slowdown yet but flagged agro risk from a possible El Nino monsoon.

guidance_outlook: Volume growth guided at 5-10% for the next year, in line with expected industry growth of about 5-7%; value growth higher because of elevated prices.
Management expects some margin improvement next year, but says it is difficult to predict continued growth beyond that.
Raw material and finished goods prices are not expected to return to pre-February 2026 levels soon; supply-chain normalisation is expected to take 3-6 months.
Kurkumbh project commissioning slipped to the beginning of Q2 FY27 from April-June 2026; mechanical completion expected by end-June; economics unchanged.
FY27-28 capex estimated at INR80-90 crore, mainly the balance of the Dahej new product plant and engineering projects; maintenance capex INR20-30 crore per year.
A product launch from the R&D pipeline is expected in July 2026; further R&D investment decisions deferred until volatility settles.
capex_capacity: Capacity utilisation at most plants is about 60-85%; enough capacity for the next few years without new investment in existing products.
Ethylamines: large plant built 3-4 years ago, adequate for 4-5 years of growth; debottlenecking possible.
Acetonitrile: about 30,000 tons capacity across two plants, sufficient for a couple of years. Balaji is building an 18,000 ton ACN plant this year.
Kurkumbh project delayed by about one quarter; mechanical completion expected end-June 2026.
Dahej new product plant: remaining spend in FY27 within the INR80-90 crore capex plan.
demand_pricing: Ammonia supply was disrupted for a week or two in March 2026, but sourcing recovered and inventories covered the gap; ammonia contracts are now short-term because suppliers are reluctant to commit longer.

Price increases have been passed through, with customers absorbing them because the company's products are a minor (C-item) cost in their bill of materials. Management believes competition, not customers, is the main pricing pressure.
Margin widening from inventory of cheaper raw materials is temporary; management expects margins to settle at competitive levels after one to two months.
Chinese imports of acetonitrile fell after Chinese players raised prices; the anti-dumping duty took effect only towards end-FY26.
Methylamines face overcapacity after Aarti's commissioning; ethylamines margins have recovered.
Peptides and acetonitrile demand expected to grow, but the company sees much of the optimistic peptide demand forecasts as unproven.

qa_highlights.question: How has user demand held up after raw material-driven price increases, and what is expected next?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has not yet seen demand destruction. Its products are a minor cost for customers, so pressure is expected from competition rather than customers. Prices are unlikely to revert to pre-February levels soon.

qa_highlights.question: Is ammonia available broadly across the industry, and how does this affect spreads?
qa_highlights.answer: Ammonia rose from about INR50/kg to over INR100/kg. Government allocation is expected, as aliphatic industry needs only 10,000-15,000 tons per month. Stabilisation is expected in 3-6 months, and any spread gain is temporary.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for capacity utilisation and the Balaji and Aarti capacity additions?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation is 60-85%. Methylamines are overcapacity after Aarti's entry, which is expected to take a long time to absorb. Ethylamines have adequate capacity for 4-5 years. Balaji's 18,000 ton ACN plant will add competition, but the company believes it is the lowest-cost producer.

qa_highlights.question: What is the planned capex for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is about INR80-90 crore, mainly completing the Dahej plant and engineering projects. Apart from this, there is no major planned capex for existing products; maintenance capex is about INR20-30 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company diversifying ammonia sourcing or looking at green ammonia?
qa_highlights.answer: Ammonia is bought mainly through distributors linked to fertiliser plants, with direct manufacturer links in only one or two cases. Green ammonia is still 3-5 years away from cost parity.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin improvement is structural versus temporary?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects some margin improvement next year. It noted that margins widen temporarily when raw material prices rise and fall, and that the company cannot predict whether it will keep growing.

risks_watch: Ammonia availability and price, with contracts now short-term and the Middle East war (Hormuz Strait) unresolved.
Demand response to 30-40% higher prices; agro demand at risk from a possible El Nino monsoon.
Methylamines overcapacity after Aarti's entry, with no near-term recovery expected.
Balaji's 18,000 ton acetonitrile plant and possible Chinese re-entry as import pricing normalises.
Pass-through reversal: competition may pull prices down faster than costs fall, reducing the temporary margin gain.
Kurkumbh commissioning timing (Q1 to Q2 FY27) and R&D product launch in July 2026.
summary.management_tone: Cautiously optimistic on margins and the price cycle, but guarded on volume and the war's duration. Management was candid that FY26 was flat and that many new products are on hold until volatility settles. It declined to give product-level tonnage or new product detail.
key_quotes: So I suspect though the prices have risen, they will not go back to the pre-February prices very soon.
Yes, I'm optimistic that we are likely to see better times in the future.
And we suspect that we will be the lowest cost manufacturer in this product for some time to come.

growth.why: Management guides 5-10% volume growth in FY27 (industry about 5-7%), plus higher value from elevated prices and some margin improvement, backed mainly by price pass-through, Chinese import share gains and the Kurkumbh and Dahej projects, but no firm new-capacity volume numbers were given beyond these projects.
